text:
sre-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — severity P1
sre-bot: summary=Capacity-tier routing misbind: hosted requests for tenant=acme-inc were routed to dedicated pool 'dedicated-eu-prod' due to fallback policy selecting wrong variant; tenant isolation temporarily bypassed; observed increased 5xx rate and latency spike. page=oncall
priya: @sam paging — you're oncall. seeing 503 spikes & requests hitting dedicated pools that shouldn't. can you ack? :rotating_light:
sam: acked. pulling logs now. working hypothesis: routing policy fallback order picked a variant tag 'eu-quant' which is only allowed in dedicated, but hosted fallback allowed it. starting triage.
elena: tagging in infra: this is causing eviction storms in dedicated pools. we had 3 pods evicting in the last 2m. metrics: dedicated-gpu-util at 95%, hosted 30%.
tom: any recent deploys to routing service? deploy-bot shows no prod deploys in last 6h.
sam: running query on request router logs: `select count(*) from routed_requests where tenant='acme-inc' and pool='dedicated-eu-prod' and status!='ok' group by minute` — lots of errors around 2145678800-2145678900.
priya: customer-impact check: @customer-success can you check if acme-inc reported errors? which customers affected?
customer-success: acme-inc reported chat sessions failing and a latency spike. also BoxRunner (tenant=box-run) saw elevated latency but less errors. tracking outreach.
marta: console snapshot: routing policy for workload-class=hosted had a new fallback list that includes model_variant:eu-quant — that's wrong. policy id=policy-37b2. looks like a policy rollout from last night.
sam: found config change in git: `infra/routing/policies/policy-37b2.yaml` changed via PR #4829 (author: infra-ops). snippet:
```
fallbacks:
  - model_variant: eu-quant
  - model_variant: eu-std
```
this entry didn't include `deployment_scope: dedicated-only` and so hosted accepted it.
elena: so hosted accepted a dedicated-only variant. that's the tenant isolation leak. we need immediate mitigation: block eu-quant from hosted routing.
priya: quick mitigation options: 1) patch policy to remove eu-quant from hosted and reapply (fast) 2) add temporary routing deny rule for model_variant=eu-quant in hosted route table 3) scale dedicated pool to absorb load (slow)
sam: I'm going to apply option 2 now via admin-api: `POST /admin/routing/overrides` body `{ "scope": "hosted", "deny_variant": "eu-quant", "note": "emergency - tenant isolation leak" }` — doing it.
sam: (logs) admin-api responded 200. override id=ovr-2145. verifying routing decisions...
elena: checking dedicated CPU/GPU load. slowly dropping. evictions stopped 40s ago.
tom: checking request flow on proxy: confirmed responses from hosted edge no longer routed to dedicated for acme-inc. good.
customer-success: acme-inc confirms errors subsiding, says most chats recovered. BoxRunner still seeing some degraded latency but generally ok.
priya: escalation/hand-off: @sam you will lead mitigations; @elena you own infra stabilization; @marta you own config rollback and PR audit. I'll coordinate customer comms and postmortem.
sam: oncall -> incident lead. starting deeper root cause: why did policy allow eu-quant into hosted fallback list? searching PR #4829 changes...
marta: PR shows ops engineer added a global fallback template; accidentally used a template variable `{{fallback_variants}}` that pulled in dedicated-only variants. looks like missing validation in CI.
priya: immediate next steps: - keep override in place - open hotfix PR to policy-37b2 to explicitly scope eu-quant to dedicated-only - add CI lint to fail on variants with annotation 'dedicated-only' used in hosted policies
elena: scaling note: temporary autoscale added to dedicated to handle spill, but we should revert once traffic normalized to avoid cost. set target down at T+30m.
tom: monitoring: dashboards updated: panel 'tenant-isolation breaches' showing 1 active; added alert to notify if fallback to dedicated occurs for hosted tenants.
customer-success: doing customer outreach: 1) acme-inc notified SLA impact and mitigation. 2) BoxRunner informed of transient latency and steps taken. both request postmortem.
sam: running a small audit: list tenants routed to dedicated in last 60m where tenant.affinity==hosted. returning: ["acme-inc", "box-run", "marketplace-inc"] — need to notify.
priya: assign action items: - sam: full routing audit & timeline (due in 2h) - marta: hotfix PR + CI lint (30m) - elena: infra scaling revert plan (1h) - tom: update dashboards/alerts (15m) - customer-success: sent notices + schedule postmortem invite (45m)
sam: starting commands: `kubectl logs router-ubuntu-01 -n prod | grep "tenant=acme-inc" | tail -n 200` -> saving logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/2145678901/.
marta: creating PR now -> https://git.internal/repo/policy/PR/4892 (hotfix). adding reviewers @infra-team.
priya: good. keep this thread for live updates. once stabilised we'll create incident board and link postmortem. please add timeline entries.
elena: infra checks healthy; evictions gone; GPU util back to 68%.
sam: audit in progress. preliminary root cause: lack of validation in policy templating allowed dedicated-only variant to be included by mistake.
customer-success: acme-inc has accepted interim workaround, asks for ETA on full fix and postmortem.
priya: ETA for hotfix + CI lint is 30-45m, postmortem will be prepared after incident closure. I'll draft customer note and share.
sam: final checks: replay routing decisions for 2145678800-2145679000 and confirm no further misroutes after override. all clear.
sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity-> mitigated; continue monitoring in this thread; create postmortem tikcet (TKT-2145) and assign to priya.
priya: assigning postmortem. closing page, keeping thread as incident record. :white_check_mark:
